notes.meaning: When God brought his people home from captivity in Babylon, it felt so wonderful that they thought they were dreaming. Conquering empires back then almost never let exiled nations go home, so this sudden freedom was an astonishing surprise. It showed the people that the Lord is always faithful to keep his ancient promises.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writer Augustine taught that Babylon represents this fallen world, and that the return pictures Christ rescuing sinners from bondage to sin.

notes.meaning: The unexpected rescue filled the returned captives with bursting laughter and songs of praise. Even foreign nations who worshipped other gods saw what happened and admitted that the Lord had done great wonders for his people. When God rescues his people, his goodness becomes a clear witness to the whole world.

The worshippers joyfully repeat what the surrounding nations had said. They gladly acknowledge that God truly did great things for them, and it filled them with deep, settled happiness. Looking back on how God helped in the past gives his people real strength and joy for the present.

The return was not finished yet, because many Israelites were still scattered in exile and the homeland remained dry and broken. The people pray for God to bring the rest of the nation home, just like seasonal rains suddenly fill dry desert riverbeds in the south. They ask the Lord to complete the good restoration he had already started.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine followed older Latin translations that spoke of a south wind, picturing the Holy Spirit melting the icy freeze of sin so believers could rush home to God.

notes.meaning: Rebuilding the nation was painful, exhausting work, much like planting seed in hard, dry soil during hard times. Yet God promises that tearful labor done in faith will eventually turn into a joyful harvest. Believers can trust that their sorrow and hard work for God will never be in vain.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interpreted sowing in tears as doing good works and helping the poor during hardship, which God will richly reward with eternal peace.

notes.meaning: A poor farmer might walk to the field weeping because seed is scarce and the season looks bleak. Yet by keeping at it and scattering the grain, he is guaranteed to come back singing and carrying heavy bundles of wheat. God blesses faithful, patient endurance through tough times with an abundant reward.
